html:
The insurgency in Cabo Delgado began on 5 October 2017, when Islamist militants attacked police stations in Mocímboa da Praia in the far north of Mozambique.

The group, known locally as al-Shabaab and later tied to the Islamic State, drew on anger among poor young people in a province where huge offshore gas fields had been found but brought few jobs. Attacks on villages grew, and in March 2021 militants overran the town of Palma, next to a large gas project, which was halted.

Troops from Rwanda and the Southern African Development Community came in from 2021 and retook towns. Fighting continues, and about a million people have been displaced in this corner of Mozambique, on the old Swahili coast near the Island of Mozambique.
sum: The insurgency in Cabo Delgado began on 5 October 2017, when Islamist militants attacked police stations in Mocímboa da Praia in the far north of Mozambique.
